title: Can a Foreigner or Dual Citizen Own Property in Bangladesh? Rules for NRBs and Foreign Spouses
metaTitle: Can Foreigners or Dual Citizens Own Property in BD?
metaDescription: Who can own land and flats in Bangladesh? Rules for Bangladeshi dual citizens, foreign passport holders and foreign spouses, including NVR, agricultural land and permission.
keywords: can foreigner buy property in Bangladesh
heroIntro: Your passport colour changes how Bangladeshi law sees you. A Bangladeshi dual citizen, a Bangladeshi-born person who gave up citizenship, and a pure foreigner are treated very differently when they want to buy, inherit or sell property. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Who Can Own What?
points: Bangladeshi citizens, including those living abroad and most dual citizens, can own land and flats.
Foreign nationals generally cannot freely buy land and typically need government permission or a BIDA-approved investment route.
Agricultural land is more restricted; check the current rules before any purchase.
Inheritance can pass property to foreign-citizen heirs in some cases, but there are limits and procedures.
Always confirm your citizenship status and, if applicable, your NVR endorsement before you sign.

toc: Dual Citizens and the NVR Endorsement

sections.content:
• Bangladeshi citizen living abroad: keeps full property rights.
  • Bangladeshi dual citizen: holds Bangladeshi and another nationality (permitted for citizens of certain countries); rights continue if citizenship is retained with the proper endorsement.
  • Foreign national, including former Bangladeshis who renounced citizenship: treated as a foreigner for most purposes.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

sections.h2: Dual Citizens and the NVR Endorsement
sections.content: The Citizenship Act 1951 and Bangladeshi policy allow dual citizenship for citizens of specified countries. Bangladesh Missions and the Immigration authority issue a "No Visa Required" (NVR) endorsement on the foreign passport to prove citizenship at the border. Having a valid NVR makes buying, selling and mutation easier because it connects your foreign passport to your Bangladeshi identity. If you lack it, see our guide on dual citizenship and NVR.

For a pure foreign national, ownership of land is restricted. Typical routes are:

  • Government permission or a BIDA-approved project for business premises or factories.
  • Long-term lease for commercial use instead of freehold.
  • Investment through a Bangladesh company with the required approvals.
  • Flats under certain developer schemes, where allowed.

Rules change often and differ by area and land type, so do not rely on a broker's assurance. Get written advice from an advocate first.

Agricultural land is subject to special limits on who may own and how much one may hold. Many purchases by non-farmers or foreigners require permission, and conversion to non-agricultural use also needs approval. NRBs who are citizens should still check the land classification in the Khatian (see record checking guide).

A foreign spouse does not automatically gain ownership of the Bangladeshi spouse's property, but may inherit as an heir under the applicable personal law, subject to the foreigner restrictions. Put estate planning in place: a will, registered gift deeds, or properly documented joint ownership, all drafted by an advocate.

1. Confirm your citizenship status with the Bangladesh Mission.
  2. Get the NVR endorsement if you are a dual citizen.
  3. Ask an advocate whether your purchase needs permission.
  4. Check land classification and mutation record.
  5. Document your funds through bank channels.
  6. Consider a will to avoid disputes after death (see inheritance guide).

faqs.question: Can an NRB with a UK/US/Canadian passport buy land in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: If you remain a Bangladeshi citizen (with dual citizenship where allowed), you can generally buy land. If you renounced Bangladeshi citizenship, you are treated as a foreigner.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner buy a flat in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: In some cases, yes, under approvals and specific schemes, but freehold land purchase is restricted. Get legal advice.

faqs.question: Can my foreign wife inherit my Bangladeshi property?
faqs.answer: She can inherit as an heir under the personal law, but foreign ownership restrictions and procedures may apply.

faqs.question: What is NVR?
faqs.answer: The No Visa Required endorsement placed on a dual citizen's foreign passport to prove Bangladeshi citizenship.

faqs.question: Can I buy agricultural land as an NRB?
faqs.answer: It is more restricted than other land; check the current limits and approval requirements with your advocate.
